headline.purpose: The sprint name; the only h1 in the main view.

stat.purpose: The four sprint numbers, in tabular figures.

body.purpose: Chat messages, issue titles (at 500), sprint goal.

caption.purpose: Chat card bodies and meta lines; Graphite when secondary.

label.purpose: Badges, counts and statuses. Never uppercase, never above a heading.

mono.purpose: Identifiers: issue keys, tool names, versions, stages, error codes, logs.

shadows.name: surface-ring
shadows.purpose: Hairline that separates board cards and stat cards instead of a border or shadow.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: The halo half of keyboard focus on buttons, inputs and badges, paired with a solid 1px border in --ring (Graphite; Pencil in dark), which carries the 3:1. Disclosures and the focusable scroll regions take a solid 2px --ring outline instead (inset on the board pane and the chat scroller).

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Colour, background and ring changes on buttons, badges and inputs.

motion.name: progress-fill
motion.purpose: Deployment progress bar advancing a whole stage.

motion.name: liveness-pulse
motion.purpose: Typing dots and a running tool.

narrative.overview:
DevSprint is a quiet control room for a sprint. Two panes sit side by side with no chrome between
them but a hairline: the board on the left and the copilot on the right, so cause and effect are
always in the same view. The room is drawn in ink and paper. Every surface, word and divider is a
step on one zero-chroma ramp, so the eye rests until something needs it. Colour is a signal, not a
mood. It appears where a stage succeeds, a write fails, or a data line traces the sprint, and
nowhere else.

Density is calm, not cramped. Workspace chrome sits at 14px and chat cards at 12px, with one
typeface throughout. Monospace marks anything that is an identifier, and tabular figures keep
every number in its column. Surfaces are flat. They are separated by 1px rings at 10% opacity and
by tonal steps, never by drop shadows at rest. Corners are gently rounded, from 8px on chat cards
to 14px on board cards, and the system is meant to feel soft and approachable, not clinical: the
next layer of work warms the interactions rather than adding ornament.

The system is fully themed. Light is paper with ink, and dark is ink with paper. Both are tokens
on `:root` and `.dark`, toggled by a class on `<html>`, and both must hold WCAG 2.2 AA.

- One neutral ramp at zero chroma carries the whole interface; hue appears only as a signal.
- Flat surfaces: hairline rings and tonal steps, no shadows at rest.
- One typeface (Geist), with monospace for identifiers and tabular figures for numbers.
- State is always a word, code or glyph first, and a colour second.
- Gently rounded, soft forms (6 to 14px, and pills for badges).
keyCharacteristics: One neutral ramp at zero chroma carries the whole interface; hue appears only as a signal.
Flat surfaces: hairline rings and tonal steps, no shadows at rest.

rules.name: The Signal-Only Rule
rules.body: Hue means something happened: success, failure, or measured data. Chrome, layout and decoration stay on the ink-and-paper ramp.

rules.name: The Word-First Rule
rules.body: Every state is legible in greyscale. Colour sits on a label ("failed", "awaiting approval"), an error code, or a stage glyph (○ ◐ ● ✕ –), never on its own.

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: If it is an identifier, it is monospace. If it is a number in a list or a stat, it uses tabular figures.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: At rest, a surface is separated by a ring or a tone, never by a shadow. A shadow, if it ever appears, is a reaction to a pointer or keyboard state.

dos: Do keep chrome on the ink-and-paper ramp, and reach for Go Green, Stop Red or Trace Blue only when a result or a measurement is being shown.
Do pair every state with a word, code or glyph, so it reads in greyscale.
Do set identifiers in monospace and numbers in tabular figures.
Do separate surfaces with a 1px ring at 10% or a tonal step, and keep 14px corners for board cards and 8px for chat cards.

Do spend the Ink-filled button once per region, on the affirmative action, and use outline for everything secondary or abortive. Several open approval cards in one message are one region: only the first undecided card's Approve is Ink.
Do check every change in both themes at WCAG 2.2 AA.

Do theme the browser's own surfaces: `color-scheme` per theme, an ink-tint selection, Rule-coloured scrollbars, a `theme-color` that follows the chosen theme (not only the OS), and the theme applied before first paint.
donts: Don't put a drop shadow on a surface at rest.
Don't add hue for decoration or branding until a single brand accent has been chosen deliberately.
Don't hard-code a colour. Every signal is a token (`--success`, `--destructive`, `--chart-1`), and a new colour arrives as a token in both themes or not at all.
Don't wrap an OKLCH token in `hsl()`. Mix with `color-mix(in oklch, …)`.

Don't add motion without a `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback. Pulses stop, the progress fill jumps (`motion-reduce:`) and a changed board card's ring holds still, and the state word or the static mark still carries the meaning.
Don't put a label or eyebrow above a heading.
Don't render model text as HTML or links. Chat text uses the safe subset only.
